$comment: D-CSUBSET-POINTER-DIFF-EDGE-CASES part (2): a MISMATCHED-pointee pointer difference. MEASURED 2026-09-01, each reference probed SEPARATELY at -O0 AND -O2: gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 REJECT `char* - int*`, but MSVC 19.51.36252 (/std:c17) COMPILES it with warning C4133 'from int * to char *'. The disjunction settles accept-vs-refuse, so DSS accepts and WARNS (S_PointerDifferenceIncompatiblePointee) rather than erroring — the row's stated 'emit a loud diagnostic' was refuted by the measurement. C4133's own wording gave the MEANING: MSVC converts the RIGHT operand to the LEFT's type, so the stride is sizeof(*LEFT) — MEASURED from MSVC's /FAs listing at /O2, `char* - int*` emits a bare sub (stride 1), `int* - char*` emits sub;sar 2 (stride 4), `double* - char*` emits sub;sar 3 (stride 8). The three strides here are DIFFERENT from each other, so no single hardcoded stride satisfies the example, and each wrong stride yields its own exit code. The second half pins CONTEXT-INDEPENDENCE: before P48 the identical expression compiled in a cast context and failed S_TypeMismatch in an initializer or argument context. RED-ON-DISABLE: revert the mismatched-pointee arm in the semantic combineBinary and the ptrSub widening in cst_to_hir -> `long n = ca - ib;` and `sink(ca - ib)` fail S_TypeMismatch and this example does not COMPILE.
